The resulting identity is 48+2 times three nonnegative squared moduli. Simultaneous zero solutions are exactly two cube-root triples; triangle inequalities characterize the upper endpoint. A parity obstruction yields the sharp binary 54. Algebraic alphabet divisibility and exact difference injectivity for finite grids complete the scope. Embedded checker independently reproduces the lattice-convolution calculations and all 35 normalized binary/ternary cases; finitary tests are supplemental, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The complete total-degree-two simplex is a canonical natural 2D six-character aperture. Its three multi-pair autocorrelations interact; simultaneous cubic-root cancellation is a meaningful sharp constraint, not a renamed standard inequality. The exact phase orbit geometry, sharp integrated sidelobe/merit factor 3, strict binary gap (best merit factor 2), and q-alphabet divisibility criterion are natural reproducible invariants. These facts can inform exact small-aperture phase-code design and do not require an unsupported global construction theorem.
